newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.

* Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Monday as bonds and gold prices eased. * Analysts said markets should remain stable ahead of July 1-2 U.S. Federal Reserve meeting.
Toronto stocks were expected to follow U.S. markets lower at the open on Monday after a triple-witching Friday, as gold and bond prices fell.
MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said New York markets will likely reverse the gains made during Friday's triple-witching.

"This expected negative activity in the U.S. market will hurt us. Gold is down... not a lot but it continues to slide. Our bonds are under modest pressure, European stock markets are under pressure. There's just a lot of things that point down," Beattie said.
But Beattie said both Canada and the U.S. remain in a strong uptrend that should limit losses.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost about a point on Friday to close at 6511.43 after the gold sector shed nearly three percent.
Beattie said trading should remain stable this week in the absence of major economic data, and investors are not expecting the U.S. Federal Reserve to hike interest rates at its July 1-2 meeting.

"The market is widely expecting no change in (Fed) policy, and I don't think there is any data this week that would cause the people to say say 'Oh oh, the Fed is going to have to rise.' We've already gotten the key data out of the way," Beattie said.

In economic news, Statistics Canada said today that foreign investors bought a net C$4.18 billion of Canadian securities in April, after selling a net C$2.28 billion in March (revised from C$2.14 billion).
The agency said Canadian residents bought a net C$291 million of foreign securities after buying C$1.76 billion in March (revised from C$2.11 billion).

* Unionized workers at Bombardier Inc's de Havilland unit are set to walk off the job at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT on Monday unless a tentative agreement can be reached between the Canadian Auto Workers union and de Havilland. Contract talks were continuing and a CAW news conference was scheduled for 0930 EDT/1350 EDT.
